verify_r95_review.py.description: Standard-library deterministic audit of the pinned R95 tables, source identities and release ledgers.

blocking_findings: The measured work gain is shared by quadratic, spline and ReLU continuations and is not neural-specific.
The representation comparison is not matched by effective rank, approximation budget, training work or serialized complexity.
The 1/16 equivalence margin lacks external economic calibration and is large relative to the observed effects.
The paired intervals establish only containment within a broad margin, not close equivalence at the scale of observed differences.
Complete work and amortization are not identified from repeated processes or multiple architectures.
The executed experiment is two-date, two-state and scalar-control.
The primary local freeze was not remotely timestamped before evaluation.
Independent validation is kernel-level rather than full-stack.
The formal release workflow and tests gate fail.
The strongest certificate comparison is post-evaluation.
The cumulative submission spans 56 article pages, 56 supplement pages and 178 appendix pages.
The method does not yet change an economically consequential conclusion.
major_required_changes: Repair the preservation ledger and publish a fully green immutable release.
Run a rank- and cost-matched representation frontier with strong non-neural stored baselines.
Freeze and publish a genuinely independent confirmation protocol before execution.
Motivate and power an economically meaningful equivalence margin.
Report a complete acquisition-and-reuse break-even frontier.
Strengthen timing evidence with repeated processes and another architecture.
Execute the nested-risk method on a vector or longer-horizon problem.
Independently implement the full endpoint and inference chain.
Make certificate construction a prospective algorithmic ablation.
Supply an economically consequential calibration or application.
Compress the active submission while retaining the historical archive.
positive_findings: R95 creates a coherent continuous-law theorem--algorithm--evidence chain under nested AVaR.
The original-optimum certificate covers the full action interval and the implemented terminal controller.
All 16,384 arm-state records meet the common qualification targets.
Stored continuations reduce the completed local evaluation workload by roughly 62 to 65 percent.
ReLU obtains the tightest whole-square residual enclosures at both risk levels.
All twelve comparisons are interpreted correctly as broad-margin equivalence rather than superiority.
The paper preserves negative screening results, interrupted attempts and verification boundaries.
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not continue the cumulative manuscript through another ordinary revision round. Encourage a new focused submission centered on certified stored continuations under recursive risk after the release defect, budget-matched comparison, economic calibration and independent confirmation are completed.

not_performed: No new fits, policy evaluations, timings or economic observations were created.
The 302 MB workflow artifact was not downloaded and rerun.
The proofs were reviewed manually but not formalized in a proof assistant.
The full production stack was not independently reimplemented.
performed: Pinned the current branch head and source identities.
Reviewed the active manuscript, supplement, appendix, response, central R95 theory and evidence sections.
Checked all principal R95 tables, the release manifest, workflow steps and complete test ledger.
Recomputed table-level speedups, interval widths, equivalence checks and release-test counts.
Created a deterministic audit script for a full repository checkout.
